quest.title: Fight for Academic Reputation!
quest.description: You meet a familiar-looking researcher sighing by the side of the road. Go ask him what's wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME}, this guy's laughing and crying at the same time... and he looks pretty familiar, doesn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Ah! It's been a while, you two. Do you still remember me?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: It's me, Jami from Amurta! Inventor of the Fayz Potion! You know me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon thinks she remembers you now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is your research going well, then?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Haha... Well... *sigh*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like that's a "no."

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: No, no, thanks to you, my Fayz Potion research achieved rather impressive results.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But I was so worried about disappointing my mentor... I never expected him to praise my work to the skies.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: "Ah, Jami, well done! A student I am proud of, indeed!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. Isn't that a good thing?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: It would have been good if we had just stopped there, sure... But what happened afterward was a true nightmare.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And what happened, exactly?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Maybe the data we got was *too* ideal, because my mentor, that smiling old fella with a wrinkly smile, got it into his head to "try it himself."

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: So, I set the experimental site for him, and brewed up the most effective of Fayz Potions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And...?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: And then... Under the watchful eyes of countless students, he boldly stood right in front of the monsters while drinking the potion and got ambushed for his trouble. They beat him in the blink of an eye...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Fortunately, he's fine. He just needs some bed rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pfft, hahaha!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Hehe... *cough* Regardless, it was my lack of academic proficiency that embarrassed my mentor.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: That ill-tempered fogey then proceeded to blame me all the more for "not considering user needs" and "lacking awareness of practical circumstances." It was a real tongue-lashing, I'll tell you that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that's unreasonable! He's to blame too!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Right? Anyway, that's why I'd like you two to—

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: No, no! I've got no such ill intentions! Not right now, anyway!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you've had them "before," have you?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Uh... That's... not super important right now.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: What I mean to say is that after reviewing previous experiments, I have come up with a "Long-Lasting Fayz Potion."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, and what's that supposed to do?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I recalled my mentor's reaction when he was ambushed, and I suddenly realized that we ordinary people tend to freeze up in the face of danger, at a loss as to what to do...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: If you only drink the potion when you're already in danger, it might have no time to work on you.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But this version is different. Once you've drunk it, it will trigger once you encounter danger, which can buy more time for normal folks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How can you tell if you're "in danger"?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Didn't I say so earlier? Ordinary people will lock up when danger approaches. As long as you act normally after drinking the Long-Lasting Fayz Potion, it will not take effect.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But once they freeze on the spot, the potion will kick in, slowing their "subjective" time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so that's how it works. Paimon kinda gets it now. In that case... Are you asking us to help you complete your experiment?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: That's right. Although the Long-Lasting Fayz Potion was designed for ordinary people, experiments can still be risky, so it would be best to have someone with combat experience do the initial testing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, let Paimon think. Should we help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ooh, Paimon's suddenly a little hungry. We could use a meal at Lambad's Tavern, don't you think, {NICKNAME}? Do we have enough Mora for that?

choices.text: Hate to break it to you...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: *cough* Well, to tell the truth, despite the tongue-lashing, my mentor did grant me a considerable amount of research funding. I would be willing to pay handsomely...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, let us lend you our aid!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Thank you so much! Please, save me from my shattered academic reputation!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Oh, so you remember that nickname... Yeah, it's me, Jami, the sighing Amurta researcher, shame of my school, and ashamed to this day to speak my name—
